title: Ranzo's code, 1528: the letter to 'Garbino' (BnF fr. 3022 no. 20, Madrid 11 April 1528) and Hieronimo Ranzo's letters (fr. 2988 ff. 2, 9-10; DECODE R1894, R4450)

steps.what: Fetched fr. 3022 (Gallica btv1b90601558) and identified the three catalogue pieces and folios.
Found no. 10 already solved by Lasry (2023) with Tomokiyo's edited text (2026), and Lasry's 2026 preliminary decryption of Cipher 2 covering no. 6 and no. 19.
Transcribed no. 20 (1,315 groups) and ~2,600 groups of Ranzo's signed letters in fr. 2988; addition sheet transcribed (additione.json).
No. 20 code is initial letter + number, the number running in alphabetical order within each letter (solve.py, anchor.py).
Word annealer (solve2.py) on a held-out 3,900-word Castiglione control encoded the same way: ~46 % token, ~9 % type accuracy.
solve2.py on no. 20 + Ranzo: a stable function-word skeleton (che, il, per, non …) across six restarts; no content words.

Sought cribs: Clair. 327 and Clair. 314 copies (undeciphered), fr. 2988 other cipher pieces (a different French cipher), fr. 3019 no. 27 Ranzo letter (no decipherment), no duplicate text between no. 20 and Ranzo letters.
DECODE R1894 (catalogue 170) identified as the fr. 2988 Ranzo letter already transcribed; no key or decipherment on the record.

Contributed research history: George Lasry, collaborating with Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, reconstructed a working Ranzo key from Norbert Biermann’s five-letter transcription. Selected values were checked against the historical addition. The Codex consolidation retains tentative proposals; this is dated source history, not work newly done on 14 October.

A Cryptoole alert (IT1520-1, solved 6 Oct 2026 by Paolo Rosson and George Lasry) led to Rosson's page and files (key/table.tsv, reading/islands.md, decode.py). Their reading uses this project's transcription for fr. 3022 no. 20 and fr. 2988, and a new transcription of the duplicate fr. 3019 ff. 73-74. No. 20 was not unread for lack of a key after all.

Applied Rosson's 779-value key (with his transcription corrections) to n20/f44r-f46v and ranzo_c006-c020. Groups with a value (sure, probable, null): no. 20 93.8%, R1894 (c017-c020) 97.2%; in runs of six or more sure/probable values: no. 20 79.8%, R1894 93.1%. Spot check: c017 and c020 decode as coherent 1528 Italian. Below the 95% bar on the connected-stretch measure; 84 groups of 3,903 have no value. Did not rerun their blind controls.

Prepared the Codex consolidation for contribution: reproduced 541 line-aligned readings, 6,428 cipher occurrences, all 871 key frequencies and two precisely bounded excerpts with translations. Checked the Cryptiana contemporaneous reports. Coverage includes hypotheses and is not measured plaintext correctness.

Split the combined catalogue item 7 target after George Lasry pointed out that it mixed different ciphers: del Vasto's no. 6 (Cipher 2, shifted letters with code groups; sibling no. 19) stays in vasto1527; no. 20 and the Ranzo letters (initial-letter code with numbered word lists) moved to ranzo1528; no. 10 (Cipher 1, read by Lasry and Tomokiyo, not reworked) is a cross-reference only. This folder takes no. 20, the Ranzo transcriptions, Rosson's measure and Lasry's contributed edition.

Tested George Lasry's correction that the addition sheet (fr. 3022 f. 50, additione.json) is not this code's key: of its 113 groups only g217 occurs (once) in the 3,912 transcribed groups of no. 20 and Ranzo's letters, and its numbers overlap the letters' own (b from 157 vs b up to 215 in the letters). The 18 Sept claim that it continues the base lists is withdrawn; page and NOTES corrected.

profile.documents extended to the five letters of George Lasry's package (fr. 2988 f. 2, fr. 2988 ff. 9-10 = R1894, fr. 3022 no. 20, fr. 4050 ff. 79-81, fr. 6638 pp. 67-70), counts from his counts.json; fr. 4050 and fr. 6638 not seen here.

outcome.method_basis: This project's own word-substitution annealer recovered only function words. Paolo Rosson's key (6 Oct 2026, with Claude, on this project's transcription) gives values to 93.8% of no. 20's groups and 97.2% of R1894's, 79.8% and 93.1% in connected stretches of sure or probable values. George Lasry's independent key (6 Oct 2026, on Biermann's transcription) assigns values to 95.9% of the non-null occurrences of five letters.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Rosson's key applied to this project's transcriptions (measure_rosson.py, 14 Oct 2026): groups in runs of six or more sure/probable values, no. 20 1,046 of 1,311 (79.8%), R1894 1,654 of 1,776 (93.1%); together 2,700 of 3,087. A reading by others, not this project's.

gaps.item: No. 20 and R1894 (fr. 2988 ff. 9-10): 84 groups without a value and 76 guesses in 3,903 parsed groups
gaps.detail: Rosson's key leaves 86 groups unvalued by his count; stems and numbers 6-9 spelling signs remain. Needs a comparison of their readings with the images, and the other Ranzo letters (fr. 2988 ff. 2r-v, fr. 3019 f. 73 duplicate) transcribed.

outcome.notes: Read in part by others: Rosson (with Claude) and George Lasry (with Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra), both 6 Oct 2026. Lasry's Biermann-based five-letter edition in lasry/: 6,428 cipher occurrences, 871 proposed mappings, 5,967/6,221 non-null occurrences assigned including hypotheses; coverage, not a plaintext accuracy estimate. Split 14 Oct 2026 from targets/vasto1527.
